about: A bookshelf at the foot of a block

lines.text: When Mdm Rosnah first placed a small bookshelf at the foot of her block,
she did not expect anyone to notice it. Within a month, however, the shelf has
lines.note: Tense: the story is in the past, so it is 'had grown'.

lines.text: grown into a corner library with more than three hundred book. Residents of
all ages now drop by after dinner, and much of them have become regular
lines.note: 'Many' goes with people you can count; 'much' does not.

lines.text: visitors. The rules are simple: take a book, read it, and return it when you
are done. Nobody keeps a record, yet very few books have went missing so
lines.note: Verb form: after 'have' it is 'gone', not 'went'.

lines.text: far. Mdm Rosnah believes that people behave good when they are trusted.
lines.note: Word form: 'behave' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'well'.

lines.text: Last year, a group of students offered to help she sort the books by
subject. They also painted the shelves and add a reading bench for the
lines.note: Tense: 'painted … and added' — both verbs are in the past.

lines.text: elderly. What began as one woman’s hobby is now a meeting place who brings
lines.note: 'Who' is for people. A place takes 'that' or 'which'.

lines.text: neighbours together. Similar shelves have since appeared at three other blocks
in the estate, each one looked after by the people who live there.
